summary: A speculative news-style piece describes 'The Ashen Plague,' a series of volcanic eruptions starting September 5, 2023 that inject ash and sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere and trigger a volcanic winter. It covers the hit to aviation, agriculture, energy, manufacturing, financial markets and insurance, with quotes from various experts. Global economic impact could reach trillions of dollars, and recovery may lag the physical winter.
one_line: Fictional-style news report on a global volcanic winter, 'The Ashen Plague,' and its economic shocks across aviation, agriculture, energy, manufacturing, markets and insurance.
key_facts: The eruptions began on September 5, 2023 and were dubbed 'The Ashen Plague.'
The chain started with the eruption of Mount Tambora 2.0, described as a hypothetical successor of the 1815 eruption.
Later eruptions involved Mount Vesuvius, Iceland's Katla volcano, and Yellowstone Caldera.
AirFinance analyst James McHale estimated aviation lost about $15 billion in the first month.
Dr. Anita Gardner of the Global Food Security Institute warned of substitute scrambles, commodity hoarding and possible rationing.

Dr. Edward Rivers of the Pallas Climate Observatory said the current events could exceed historical precedents, possibly causing years of reduced temperatures; the 'Year Without a Summer' in 1816 followed Tambora's eruption.
Solar power suffers because ash clouds reduce sunlight penetration, while Michelle Torres of EnergyVista Inc. expects wind, geothermal and hydroelectric development to accelerate.
Professor Lewis Feldman of Monarch University said disruptions affect raw material sourcing, with soil and water contamination, and cold, dark operating conditions.
Automotive, electronics and pharmaceutical industries are especially vulnerable due to just-in-time delivery schedules.
The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average shed significant points since the eruptions began.
Financial advisor Emily Chan advises clients to reevaluate portfolios and consider traditional 'safe haven' commodities.
Insurers estimate costs in the multiple billions of dollars; Selena Gomez of SecureFuture PLC says tail risks must be integrated into actuarial models.
Estimated global economic impact could reach trillions of dollars, and central banks and governments are issuing stimulus and easing monetary policy.
